thread:
maya (support): heads up — customer ACME reported a sudden p99 increase from ~350ms to ~1.1s starting ~09:22 UTC after we pushed the compact-coalesce tuning change. They see timeouts in some interactive flows.

sam (eng-sre): thanks, can you paste the tenant id + example request id? any pattern on prompt length or token counts?

maya (support): tenant=acme-prod, req_id=01F8Z9ABX, short prompts (<=10 tokens) mostly, but a few mid-size. stack traces show requests stuck in batcher hold path waiting for coalesce timeout.

anya (oncall): grabbing logs now. Querying batcher metrics for that host group.

sre-bot: deploy "compact-coalesce-v2" rolled at 09:15 UTC on pool gpu-prod-6. Flag: continuous_batching.coalesce_timeout_ms=40 -> 20, max_batch_size=32 -> 48.

lee (eng-runtime): changing coalesce_timeout_ms that low can increase tail when many tiny requests arrive — they miss the short-latency path. Did we also enable immediate_flush_small_requests?

sam (eng-sre): not in that rollout. Looks like we lowered timeout to reduce avg cost but didn't enable small-request fast-path.

maya (support): customer sent two example request logs: 
```
# req 1
prompt_tokens=6
latency_ms=1120
batch_wait_ms=980
server=gp-06-3
```

```
# req 2
prompt_tokens=8
latency_ms=1020
batch_wait_ms=900
server=gp-06-7
```

anya (oncall): corroborating — bulk of p99 increase comes from gp-06 pool; batch_wait_ms spikes near new coalesce_timeout. p95 less affected.

sam (eng-sre): immediate mitigation: roll back the coalesce timeout to 40ms for gp-06 only and enable immediate_flush_small_requests=true. Can someone run a quick canary?

lee (eng-runtime): running hotfix now on gp-06 (canary -> gp-06-3 and gp-06-7). Commands: 
```
rdwctl rollout --pool gp-06 --flag continuous_batching.coalesce_timeout_ms=40 --flag continuous_batching.immediate_flush_small_requests=true --canary 2
```

sre-bot: hotfix started at 09:36 UTC.

maya (support): customer on standby to confirm.

anya (oncall): metrics look better at 09:42 — batch_wait_ms median dropped and p99 trending down. Can we run a quick repro loop to validate?

sam (eng-sre): repro script used: 
```
for i in {1..500}; do curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/gen -d '{"prompt":"hi","max_tokens":10}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST"; sleep 0.01; done
```
Results: with immediate_flush_small_requests=true p99 ~210ms, without it ~1.0s on this workload.

lee (eng-runtime): root cause summary: compact-coalesce-v2 reduced coalesce timeout but didn't opt-in small-request flushing; small/short prompts accumulate and hit the full timeout path leading to tail spikes on certain pools under microburst traffic patterns.

sam (eng-sre): next steps: 
- revert coalesce_timeout for gp-06 to previous value (done as canary) and monitor for 30m (action: lee)
- add integration test that simulates high-QPS tiny prompts to catch regressions (action: sam)
- update rollout checklist to require immediate_flush_small_requests toggle when lowering coalesce_timeout (action: maya + eng-releases)

maya (support): emailed ACME with status and ETA 30m for full rollback if metrics stable.

anya (oncall): will keep an eye on alerts, will escalate if p99 > 700ms again.

lee (eng-runtime): I'll open a follow-up PR to make the small-request fast-path default for coalesce_timeouts < 30ms and add observability metric for "flush_path" counts.

sam (eng-sre): thanks everyone. Recording postmortem note and the repro snippet in the ticket 4109.

maya (support): ACME confirms interactive flows back to normal at 09:50 UTC :thumbsup:

sre-bot: thread closed by oncall at 09:55 UTC after 20m stable.
